- Their pace means about 2 scheduled things a day, so there is room for roughly 16 across the trip.

candidates.title: Palazzo Massimo alle Terme
candidates.summary: National Roman Museum's finest branch: frescoes from Livia's villa, mosaics and bronzes, seen properly in a quiet morning. Lifts serve the upper floors; flat indoor floors suit the cobble concern. Exact lift and handrail details are not verified here.

candidates.title: Galleria Borghese
candidates.summary: Caravaggio and Bernini in a compact villa, entered on timed slots, so a self-guided visit stays unhurried. Slots sell out, so booking ahead is likely needed. The park approach has gravel paths; step access was not checked.

candidates.title: Galleria Doria Pamphilj
candidates.summary: Private palace collection with Caravaggio and Velázquez's Innocent X, usually calm. Audio guide rather than a group tour. Stair and lift access is not confirmed.

candidates.title: Palazzo Barberini (Gallerie Nazionali)
candidates.summary: Caravaggio's Judith, Raphael's Fornarina and Pietro da Cortona's vast ceiling. A lift exists alongside Bernini's staircase, though its current availability is unverified.

candidates.title: Capitoline Museums
candidates.summary: The original Marcus Aurelius, the Capitoline Wolf and a Forum view from the Tabularium. Reach it by the Via del Teatro di Marcello side rather than the cordonata ramp. Internal step access is uneven and not verified.

candidates.title: Centrale Montemartini
candidates.summary: Roman sculpture displayed among old power-station turbines. It is quiet, flat and unusual, and suits a returning visitor.

candidates.title: Mercato di Testaccio
candidates.summary: A covered, flat-floored neighbourhood market with food stalls for a slow browse and lunch. It avoids the cobbled crowds of Campo de' Fiori. Exact closing days are not confirmed.

candidates.title: San Luigi dei Francesi and Sant'Agostino Caravaggios
candidates.summary: Free churches holding Caravaggio's Matthew cycle and Madonna di Loreto, a short distance apart. The surrounding streets are cobbled, and step access was not checked. Opening hours vary and were not verified.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel with lift in Prati, near Lepanto or Ottaviano metro
candidatesAccepted.summary: Prati has flat, wide, mostly paved pavements rather than cobbles, step-free metro access, and is a short ride to the Vatican and Borghese collections. Ask for a lift to every floor and handrails on any internal steps. Rome is busy in October, so a double here may take most of a 350 CAD daily budget. We could not confirm the exact accessibility of any one property.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel near Termini/Esquilino with step-free access
candidatesAccepted.summary: This area is flat with asphalt streets, and is close to Palazzo Massimo's Roman collections and the Esquilino covered market. Buses and metro go everywhere from here. Choose a building with a lift from street level, because many have a few unrailed steps at the entrance. Rooms are often cheaper here than in the centre, which leaves room in the daily budget.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel in Monti near Cavour metro
candidatesAccepted.summary: Monti is a walk from the Forum, Trajan's Markets and the Baroque churches. However, many of its side streets are cobbled and sloped, so a hotel on Via Cavour or Via Nazionale keeps the walking flatter. Confirm the lift and handrails before booking. Prices are likely to stretch the budget.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel in the Salario/Pinciano area near Villa Borghese
candidatesAccepted.summary: This is a quiet residential area with paved streets, within reach of the Galleria Borghese's Caravaggios and Berninis. It suits slow mornings in one place. Taxis or buses are needed for the archaeological sites, and we could not account for how long those rides take.

candidatesAccepted.title: Lunch at Roscioli Salumeria con Cucina
candidatesAccepted.summary: A classic Roman deli-restaurant near Campo de' Fiori for carbonara, cacio e pepe and excellent cured meats and cheeses; a seated, unhurried lunch on flat ground. Dietary restrictions were not mentioned, so none are accounted for; reservations are advised.

candidatesAccepted.title: Browsing and tasting at Mercato di Testaccio
candidatesAccepted.summary: A covered, level neighbourhood market with stalls selling street food such as trapizzino and fresh pasta. It suits their interest in markets without needing a long walk on cobbles. Opening days were not checked.

candidatesAccepted.title: Trattoria dinner in Testaccio at Flavio al Velavevodetto
candidatesAccepted.summary: Traditional Roman cooking in a dining room built against Monte Testaccio, the ancient hill made of broken amphorae, which ties the meal to Roman archaeology. Step-free access was not verified, and booking is advised.

candidatesAccepted.title: Lunch at Mercato Centrale Roma, Termini
candidatesAccepted.summary: A seated food hall with many artisan counters, convenient after a morning at Palazzo Massimo, a nearby museum of Roman antiquities. It is flat and easy, and each person can choose freely; dietary needs were not stated.

candidatesAccepted.title: Aperitivo and gelato in Prati
candidatesAccepted.summary: An unhurried aperitivo followed by gelato at Fatamorgana or Gelateria dei Gracchi, on the wide, flat streets of Prati rather than cobbles. The exact venue is left flexible.

candidatesAccepted.title: ETIAS travel authorisation for Canadian passport holders
candidatesAccepted.summary: Canadians visiting the Schengen area are expected to need ETIAS once it is in force; check its status well before October 2027 and confirm both passports are valid at least three months beyond 2027-10-16. This is not clearance to travel; verify on the official EU site.

candidatesAccepted.title: Travel medical insurance for travellers aged 68 and 71
candidatesAccepted.summary: Provincial health plans cover little abroad, and premiums and pre-existing-condition rules shift sharply at these ages, so compare policies with medical evacuation and trip interruption cover. I could not account for health history, so the price band is wide.

candidatesAccepted.title: Timed-entry tickets for Galleria Borghese
candidatesAccepted.summary: Baroque painting and Bernini under one roof, with entry by mandatory reservation that sells out. It has lifts for visitors who struggle with stairs; ask about them when booking. It suits a slow morning with no guided group.

candidatesAccepted.title: eSIM or roaming plan for two phones
candidatesAccepted.summary: Mobile data for maps, taxi apps and ticket QR codes keeps cobbled detours and stair-heavy routes avoidable. An Italian or EU eSIM is usually cheaper than Canadian roaming; check phones are unlocked.

candidatesAccepted.title: Palazzo Massimo alle Terme (National Roman Museum)
candidatesAccepted.summary: A quieter alternative to the big sites, with Roman frescoes, mosaics and sculpture, set out on level galleries with lifts, and it rewards an unhurried morning. Entry band assumes a standard adult ticket per person with no senior discount for non-EU visitors. Whether every gallery has step-free access is not confirmed, so check before relying on it.

candidatesAccepted.title: Galleria Borghese
candidatesAccepted.summary: Caravaggio and Bernini in one compact villa, with timed entry that caps the crowds, which suits a slow look at Baroque painting. The band assumes a standard timed ticket per person including the booking fee, and timed slots usually need advance reservation. Slot start times, and whether there is a handrail at the entrance stairs, are not known; choose a slot after 09:00 and check access before booking.

candidatesAccepted.title: Galleria Doria Pamphilj
candidatesAccepted.summary: A private palace collection with Caravaggio and Velázquez's Innocent X, on a flat central street and usually calm. The band assumes an adult ticket per person including the audio guide, which is self-guided, so it is not a group tour. Lift availability is not confirmed.

candidatesAccepted.title: Mercato Testaccio browse and lunch
candidatesAccepted.summary: A covered neighbourhood market with level aisles and food stalls, a gentle way to do markets without cobbles. The band covers a casual market lunch and snacks for both of you, assuming a few stall dishes and drinks. Trading days and hours were not checked.
